vertical.caption: ran after a hat
vertical.edit: Same girl, same running pose and camera, centuries ago: long old-fashioned dress and apron, a straw bonnet with ribbons flying ahead of her, a thatched village and a horse and cart behind the trees.

vertical.caption: will run after a hat
vertical.edit: Same girl and pose about 1000 years ahead: shiny silver suit, glowing trainers, the hat flies ahead on a tiny propeller, a futuristic glass city and flying cars behind the trees.

horizontal.caption: to run a race
horizontal.edit: The hat is gone; she wears a plain running vest (no numbers) and bursts towards a finish tape held across the path, other runners close behind her.

horizontal.caption: to run for the bus
horizontal.edit: The hat is replaced by a red bus pulling away along a road at the edge of the park; she sprints after it with one arm stretched out, mouth open.

horizontal.caption: to run out of breath
horizontal.edit: She has stopped, bent over with hands on her knees, red-faced, tongue out, sweat drops flying, while the hat floats far away into the sky.

question: What is the girl doing?
answerWhy: True to the clip (the wind takes her hat and she chases and catches it); 'run after' is the right collocation, present continuous for the action in the still.
notes: Tenses for level A: past simple / present continuous (original) / future with will, shown by era (old village vs futuristic city). 6 images in total; 'to run out of breath' changes her pose on purpose because clarity wins. No tense row in recall: a row cannot tell the learner which tense is meant.
